To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the laminin gamma2 chain is overexpressed in colon carcinoma cells at the invasive margin of the tumour; (ii) this is caused by the synergistic activation by TGF-beta1 and HGF of the LAM2C promoter; (iii) the synergism involves two distinct promoter elements, one being the 5' AP-1 site, the other a novel site located upstream of the TGF-beta responsive element; and (iv) the synergistic promoter

TGF-beta and the HGF/c-Met signalling pathway synergistically activate the human laminin gamma 3 chain gene (LAMC2) and that this synergistic activation is mediated by different cis-elements in the promoter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of a gene encoding an extracellular matrix protein that has a role in tumour cell invasion.
the regulation of the LAMG2 gene and the expression of laminin gamma 1 chain.
the regulation of a gene that is involved in the formation of a structure that is essential to the invasive and metastatic potential of colon cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the synergy between TGF beta and HGF is mediated via different transcription factors, and that these transcription factors act on different cis-elements in the LAMC 2 gene promoter, leading to the accumulation of the laminingamma 2 chain in colon carcinoma cells.

TGF-beta 3 and HGF synergistically activate the 5' AP-1 element of the LAMG2 gene promoter and the additional upstream element, which contains a Smad binding site, and thereby result in the accumulation of the lamin gamma 2 chain.
the LAMC 2 gene, which encodes the laminin gamma2 chain, is activated by TGF-beta and by HGF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TGF-beta and the HGF signalling pathways converge on the LAMC 2 promoter to activate the expression of the laminin-5 gamma 2 chain.
the synergistic activation by HGF and transforming growth factor beta-1 (TGF beta-1) of the LAM2C2 gene encoding laminin gamma-2 chain is mediated via different elements of the promoter.
the laminin-5 gamma 2 chain is an important component of the extracellular matrix in colon carcinomas, and the accumulation of this laminin-5 component is mediated via a novel signalling mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accumulation of the laminins in the cells at invasive front is not due to an increased synthesis of all three laminin-5 subunits, but rather to a selective overexpression of one of the subunits.

a combination of growth factor signals, such as TGF-beta and/or HGF, and cytokine signalling, as exemplified by Smad3 signalling, can synergistically activate the transcription of the LAMG2 gene, leading to the accumulation of the lamin gamma 2 chain.

the synergistic activation by TGF-beta and hepatocyte growth of the LAM2C gene, which encodes the laminin gamma2 chain, is mediated via different elements in the promoter and results in an increased expression of the laminin-5 gamma2 chain relative to other laminin-3 constituent chains.
